patterns.evidence: The facility's postal address (street, city, postal_code, country) is a nested object that exists only inside the datacenter document.
A short list of plain compliance labels such as "ISO27001", a multi-valued attribute whose length varies per facility.
Holds datacenter_id of a datacenters document together with copies of its name and region_code, so cluster listings show the location without a lookup.
Node pool definitions (pool_name, instance_type, min_nodes, max_nodes) are stored only inside the cluster; no collection holds pools as documents.
Inside each embedded node pool, a list of plain availability zone names such as "fra-a" with varying length.
A list of ObjectIds, each equal to an engineers _id, naming the cluster administrators with no copied engineer data.
Plain names of installed add-ons such as "cert-manager", an ordinary multi-valued attribute of the cluster.

Keeps at most the three most recently opened incidents (by opened_at), identical to documents of the incidents collection, which holds the full set; one cluster has an older fourth incident kept only there.
Holds only a prefixed cluster id such as "CL-0412" equal to a clusters _id, without copied cluster fields.
Physical server details (vendor, model, serial_number, rack_unit) nested in the node document and stored nowhere else.
Plain role labels of the machine such as "ingress", a bounded multi-valued attribute with different lengths.
Kubernetes taint strings such as "pci=true:NoSchedule" listed as plain values describing scheduling restrictions of the node.
Holds only the prefixed id of the cluster where the incident happened, matching a clusters _id.
ObjectId of the engineer handling the incident; no engineer attributes are copied.
ObjectId of the node whose metrics are recorded, equal to a nodes _id, with nothing else copied.
Groups time-ordered host samples (sampled_at, cpu_pct, mem_pct) inside one hour bounded by window_start and window_end, with sample_count equal to the number of items.
